# Picker's Desk

> Picker's Desk turns public records into short, plain-English weekly sales leads for small local businesses in the San Francisco Bay Area. Every entry comes straight from the government agency that keeps the record: California liquor-license filings, city and county building permits, city business registrations, and county auction notices. Facts come from the record; anything that is our reading of it is labeled as such.

Picker's Desk is a trade name of Global Qwest, Inc., based in California. Contact: roger@pickersdesk.com.

Who it's for: independent businesses of about 3 to 30 people that sell to other local businesses and can't justify enterprise data software. Main audiences are commercial electrical, HVAC, refrigeration and plumbing contractors, and companies that sell to restaurants (equipment dealers, refrigeration and hood service, distributors, linen, POS, liquidators).

How it works: every business day we save full copies of the public records we track, compare them with the day before, and sort what changed into openings, ownership changes, closings and new construction. We started archiving daily in October 2026, so the history of each address grows over time.

## Reports

- [Permit Watch](https://pickersdesk.com/permits.html): Bay Area commercial build-outs and tenant improvements from city and county building permits, filtered for electrical, HVAC, refrigeration and plumbing contractors. Shows who's building, project size and value, the general contractor where listed, and whether the electrical, mechanical or plumbing work is on the permit yet ("Trades open" means it isn't on the permit yet in the city's records; it doesn't confirm the work is unawarded or open for bid). Fields a city doesn't publish are marked "not provided by the city". Available now: 30-day free trial, then $49/month for founding members (locked for as long as they stay subscribed); the standard price will be $79/month. A free pilot (no card) is also open.
- [The Turnover](https://pickersdesk.com/#turnover): Bay Area restaurants and bars opening, closing and changing hands, from California ABC liquor-license filings and city business registrations. Free weekly highlights email (free, always); the full list is the paid Turnover, Turnover Lite planned at $19/month.
- [Bay Area Public Auctions](https://pickersdesk.com/auctions.html): free calendar of county tax-defaulted property sales and government surplus vehicle and equipment auctions across the nine Bay Area counties. Dates come only from each agency's own notice.
- [Building trends](https://pickersdesk.com/trends/): free charts of permit counts by kind of work (EV chargers, solar, battery storage, heat pumps, ADUs, restaurant build-outs) for San Francisco, Chicago, Austin, Seattle, Marin County and Campbell, each place compared only with its own past. [Methodology](https://pickersdesk.com/trends/methodology.html).
- [Sample reports](https://pickersdesk.com/reports/): real sample issues.
- [Pricing](https://pickersdesk.com/#plans): Free, Turnover Lite ($19/month, planned), Permit Watch ($49/month founding), Pro ($99/month, planned: both reports, several areas, alerts, address history).

## Learn

- [Learn](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/): guides grouped by what you want to do. [Buy at a public auction](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/auctions/); [Find and work commercial jobs](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/commercial-work/); [Check a contractor](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/check-a-contractor/); [Read permit records and trends](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/records-and-trends/).
- [How to read a permit record](https://pickersdesk.com/learn/permit-records/): the stages of a permit (filed, review, issued, inspections, final), where the trades gap sits, and a glossary of the words on a record (MEP deferred, Trades open, GC, TI), each definition citing its source.
<!-- playbooks:start -->
- [Playbooks](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/): step-by-step roadmaps with a flowchart; every fact links to the official source it came from, and each cited page is re-read on a schedule.
- [Bid on a California tax-defaulted property](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/california-tax-default-property-auction.html): When property taxes go unpaid for years, the county can sell the parcel at auction. Here's how those sales work, what you actually get, and the many ways a parcel can drop out or cost more than the winning bid.
- [Check a California contractor license before you call or hire](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/check-a-california-contractor-license.html): The Contractors State License Board (CSLB) runs a free online lookup. Here is how to use it: the ways to search, the tips that make a search work, what each section of the result shows (status, bond, workers' compensation, insurance), and when the database is down.
- [Did the permit count fall, or did the record change?](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/did-the-permit-count-fall-or-did-the-record-change.html): Permit counts jump and drop for reasons that have nothing to do with demand: a city changes how it files or dates a record, or the wording and coverage shift. Here is a four-question check to run before you trust a big move in a permit chart.
- [EV-charger permits, Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025: how to read them city by city](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/ev-charger-permits-same-quarter-different-cities.html): Five places, one permit type, the same quarter a year apart. Each city is compared only with its own past, because cities count and date permits differently. Here is how to read the numbers without over-reading them.
- [Buy a work vehicle at a government auction in California](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/government-vehicle-auction-california.html): State, federal, county and city fleets sell used trucks and vans online. Here's the path from finding a sale to driving it legally: the sellers, the paperwork, the DMV steps, and the ways it goes wrong.
- [Heat-pump permits: what the record can and can't tell you](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/heat-pump-permits-what-the-record-can-and-cant-tell-you.html): Heat-pump permits, Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025, in four places. The count is useful, but only for what it measures: records that name heat pumps or mini-splits, which is not every HVAC job.
- [San Francisco: the commercial over-the-counter permit path](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/san-francisco-commercial-permit-over-the-counter.html): An example of how one commercial permit moves in San Francisco, using the city's own step-by-step page for over-the-counter (OTC) commercial projects. Stages differ by permit type and by city, so treat this as the San Francisco example, not a rule for anywhere else.
- [When a San Francisco permit runs out](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/san-francisco-permit-expiration-and-extensions.html): Permit expiration rules are set city by city, so this card covers one city: San Francisco, for applications filed on or after June 21, 2026. If you work somewhere else, find your own city's rule. Don't carry these numbers over.
- [When a permit record's description goes blank: the Marin County example](https://pickersdesk.com/playbooks/when-a-permit-record-field-goes-blank-marin-county.html): Counting permits by what the description says only works while the description is there. In Marin County, most 2026 permit records have no description. Here is what the records show, what it does to a count, and what to do about it.
- [How to find commercial electrical and HVAC work in SF and San José before it's bid](https://pickersdesk.com/blog/find-commercial-work-before-its-bid-sf-san-jose.html): Reading building permits for tenant improvements a small shop can still bid, with real examples.
<!-- playbooks:end -->

## About the data

- [About our data](https://pickersdesk.com/data.html): sources, how filings are sorted (duplicates, transfers, withdrawn applications, closings), limits, and how to report a correction.
- [Data status](https://pickersdesk.com/status.html): every source we use, when it was last checked, and what changed. Rebuilt every weekday.
- [About](https://pickersdesk.com/about.html): who runs Picker's Desk and why.
